_note: THE MILITARY FAMILY, 6 OF ~10: THE QUARTERMASTER.
The occupiers' quartermaster has been selling stolen stock back to the people it was stolen from. Take her, and take
her ledger, which is the proof the client needs. The verb is TAKE, off the woman herself. Pods come for the ledger.
Written to the delve marker set (outside entrance, centre, item markers, boss, wounded) on his ruling, so the
lint pool is EMPTY on military sites until the markers are on them (missionboard06a's note says why).
Every word holds at any military site: nothing names the site, the faction or the weather; everything the lines
point at is placed. Pay: med, capped.

place._theme: Military sites; the family's marker set.

prose.name: Bounty: The Quartermaster on <Planet>
prose.briefing: Whoever runs supplies at the <Place> has been selling stolen stock back to the people it was taken from. Her ledger proves it.
prose.card: Bounty contract. The quartermaster at the <Place> on <Planet> is wanted. Proof is required: recover her ledger. Payment on contract completion.

beats.journal: The quartermaster at the <Place> is dead. She kept a ledger, and it is still in there somewhere.
say: That's her? Now the ledger. Without it she's just someone who was rude to us.

beats.journal: The quartermaster kept every sale. Same crates, same buyers, sold twice. The ledger is mine now.
beats.name: Quartermaster's Footlocker

message.title: Quartermaster's Ledger
message.text: Every sale in a neat hand, and a column on the right for what each buyer said when they paid. Most of them said thank you.

beats.objective: Get the ledger out of the <Place>
beats.journal: I took the quartermaster down and got her ledger out of the <Place>, through the people sent down to stop it.
say: You're out with it? Then it's done. Every name in that book is about to have a very long week.

broadcast: You're at the site. The quartermaster's inside. So's her ledger, and I want both of them dealt with. She'll call for help when it starts. She always does.
_speech: On a board the broadcast waits for him at the site. Not yet heard in game; his ear decides. No names, places, factions or currency in a voiced line.
